overview: This file documents U.S. interdepartmental and Allied-occupation discussions concerning the authority and geographic jurisdiction of Japan’s newly created Maritime Safety Board. The first group of papers traces State and Army clearance of a U.S. response to French doubts about whether Japanese officers could stop and search foreign or Allied vessels in Japanese territorial waters, culminating in instructions to the U.S. member of the Far Eastern Commission that the Board acted as an authorized agent of SCAP. A later despatch and its enclosures record a British objection to an erroneous English translation of the Maritime Safety Board Law that appeared to extend its jurisdiction to “the high seas adjacent to Japan,” followed by SCAP’s reply and the Japanese government’s published correction.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on French attitude toward the Japanese Maritime Safety Board
subfiles.about: Ray seeks Allison’s approval of a draft intended to reconcile differing views within the State Department about the French position on the Japanese Maritime Safety Board.
subfiles.summary: Ray explains that the enclosed draft memorandum to the U.S. member of the Far Eastern Commission was prepared after consultation with Allison, Johnson, and Blakeslee. Its purpose was to reconcile their views concerning the French attitude toward the Maritime Safety Board. Blakeslee had approved the draft’s final paragraph, and Ray asks whether the document should also be cleared with L/M.

subfiles.title: Memorandum proposing an information paper on the French coastal-patrol statement
subfiles.about: Ray recommends circulating a U.S. information paper instead of making an oral statement in response to the French declaration on Japanese coastal patrols.
subfiles.summary: Ray reports Allison’s view that a formal French statement made in open commission required an equally public answer. Blakeslee preferred circulating a U.S. information paper, which would state the American position while leaving any renewed discussion to the French or other interested delegations. Ray submits an attached draft instruction for Allison’s approval and further clearance.

subfiles.title: Draft instruction on the authority of the Japanese coastal patrol
subfiles.about: The draft states that Maritime Safety Board officers may stop and search foreign or Allied vessels in Japanese territorial waters as authorized agents of SCAP.
subfiles.summary: The draft responds to the French delegation’s claim that internationally recognized vessel-visiting procedures during the occupation could be exercised only under SCAP jurisdiction; it also notes that the Chinese member had reserved the right to submit a position. Citing SCAPIN 996, SCAPIN 756, and SCAPIN 1218, it argues that the Maritime Safety Authority Law made the Maritime Safety Board an authorized agent of SCAP. Accordingly, its officers could stop and search foreign or Allied vessels in Japanese territorial waters under SCAP’s executive authority, and their lawful orders required obedience. The U.S. member is instructed to convey this view to the French member and others expressing similar opinions.

subfiles.title: Army concurrence in the proposed response on Japanese coastal patrols
subfiles.from: W. H. Hault, for the Secretary of the Army
subfiles.to: Department of State, attention J. Franklin Ray Jr.
subfiles.about: The Department of the Army formally concurs in the draft memorandum to the U.S. member of the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: The Army states that it concurs in the proposed memorandum concerning the French statement on the Japanese coastal patrol. The approved draft had been forwarded to the Army with Ray’s memorandum of August 16. The concurrence completed a significant part of the interdepartmental clearance process.

subfiles.title: Request for expedited Army clearance of the coastal-patrol position
subfiles.to: Colonel Lawler, Plans and Policy Group, Plans and Operations Division, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Ray asks Lawler to expedite Army review of the State Department’s draft position on the French coastal-patrol statement.
subfiles.summary: Ray notes that Claxton had identified Lawler as the Army action officer for the matter. He transmits copies of the August 13 memorandum to Allison and the draft instruction for the U.S. member of the Far Eastern Commission. In accordance with arrangements for coordinating U.S. positions during the Commission’s recess, Ray requests expedited Army review and continuing notice of the action taken.

subfiles.title: Final instruction to the U.S. member of the Far Eastern Commission on coastal patrols
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Saltzman directs the U.S. member to inform the Commission that the Maritime Safety Board acts under SCAP authority when stopping and searching vessels in Japanese territorial waters.
subfiles.summary: The final instruction recounts the French statement at the Commission’s 114th meeting on July 8, 1948. It endorses SCAP’s view that, under SCAPIN 996, 756, and 1218, the Maritime Safety Board was an authorized agent of SCAP. Its officials therefore acted under SCAP jurisdiction and executive authority when stopping or searching foreign or Allied vessels in Japanese territorial waters. The U.S. member is directed to communicate these views to the Commission’s members.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 68 on correction of the Maritime Safety Board Law translation
subfiles.from: Acting United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: The despatch reports correction of an English translation that incorrectly placed Maritime Safety Board authority on the high seas adjacent to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Acting Political Adviser alerts the Department to a discrepancy between the Japanese original of the Maritime Safety Board Law and its official English translation. The despatch encloses the United Kingdom Liaison Mission’s request for correction, SCAP headquarters’ reply, and the published erratum. It reports that the correction appeared in the belatedly published English Official Gazette for October 13, 1948, and recommends notifying the Far Eastern Commission through the Army Civil Affairs Division’s weekly information summary.

subfiles.title: British note protesting the English translation of Article 1
subfiles.from: United Kingdom Liaison Mission in Japan
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The British mission asks that the Japanese government delete an unauthorized reference to the high seas from the English translation of the Maritime Safety Board Law.
subfiles.summary: The mission observes that the English edition of Official Gazette No. 620 inserted the phrase “on the high seas adjacent to Japan” into Article 1 even though it did not appear in the Japanese text passed by the Diet. The discrepancy had previously been called to the Far Eastern Commission’s attention in paper SC305/5. The mission warns that the erroneous language was open to misconstruction and, if accurate, could provoke representations from His Majesty’s Government in the United Kingdom.

subfiles.title: SCAP reply concerning correction of Article 1
subfiles.from: Diplomatic Section, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.to: United Kingdom Liaison Mission in Japan
subfiles.about: SCAP headquarters informs the British mission that the Japanese government will publish a correction deleting the high-seas language.
subfiles.summary: The Diplomatic Section acknowledges the British note of December 6, 1948, and states that its request was referred to the Japanese government. The government reported that a correction would appear in the English edition of the Official Gazette for October 13, 1948, which had not yet been published. The announced notice directed deletion of the phrase “on the high seas” from Article 1, paragraph 1.

subfiles.title: Official Gazette erratum to the Maritime Safety Board Law
subfiles.from: Secretary of the Prime Minister’s Office
subfiles.about: The published erratum orders deletion of the words “on the High seas” from Article 1 of the Maritime Safety Board Law.
subfiles.summary: This enclosure reproduces the correction published on page 5 of the English Official Gazette for October 13, 1948. It specifies that “on the High seas” is to be deleted from Article 1, paragraph 1, of Law No. 28 of 1948 as printed in the April 27 Official Gazette. The notice is attributed to the Secretary of the Prime Minister’s Office.

interest: The file provides a compact documentary chain from internal State Department drafting and Army concurrence to the final U.S. instruction delivered within the Far Eastern Commission. It illuminates the legal fiction by which Japanese Maritime Safety Board personnel exercised coercive powers as agents of SCAP, particularly against foreign and Allied vessels during the occupation. The later papers are especially useful for showing how a few unauthorized words in an official translation could suggest a much broader high-seas jurisdiction, prompt British diplomatic concern, and require formal correction by the Japanese government.
